rationale.conceptual: The method is well-established DFT and DFPT, but computing band gap, dielectric tensors, Born charges, zone-center phonons with LO-TO splitting, elastic constants, and derived moduli requires understanding of symmetry, pseudopotentials, convergence, and the interdependence of properties. It is non-trivial and multi-faceted, though not novel.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves at least 7 sequential stages (structure setup, SCF, band structure, dielectric DFPT, phonon DFPT, elastic constants DFPT, post-processing) with dependencies between outputs (ε^∞ and Born charges feed into LO-TO splitting and static dielectric). Setting up correct ABINIT input files, executing runs, parsing outputs, and aggregating into the required JSON demands robust orchestration and tooling.

difficulty.reasoning: The task is a standard DFT/DFPT workflow using ABINIT to compute multiple physical properties of a known crystal. It requires careful setup and multi-stage execution but no novel methods. The pipeline is long and interdependent, making orchestration challenging, but the underlying methods are textbook. Resource needs are modest (small cell, CPU-only).

compute_estimate.reasoning: The 22-atom rhombohedral cell with a 50 Ha cutoff and 6×6×6 k-point mesh is a light DFT calculation that can be completed on a single CPU core in under an hour. No GPUs are needed. Memory footprint is a few GB.
